title: Compatible quotients reducing flat local depth induction by one
statement: Let φ:R→S be a flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] local homomorphism of Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local commutative rings. Set F=S/m_R S, with its quotient local structure. If depth(R)+depth(F)>0 [def-weil-pbc-depth], there are ideals J⊆m_R and K⊆m_S and a flat local map ψ:R/J→S/K commuting with the quotient maps from φ, such that depth(S)=depth(S/K)+1 and depth(R)+depth(F)=depth(R/J)+depth((S/K)/m_(R/J)(S/K))+1. All depths are depths as modules over the indicated local rings. Quotient rings are nonzero Noetherian local rings. This assertion constructs a smaller map and two depth drops, without assuming the depth formula for any map.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0338, proof, second and third paragraphs (positive-depth cases), specialized to M = R and N = S; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0338

proof.text: For any local ring A, maximalIdeal A smul top as an A-submodule of A equals maximalIdeal A and is not top. Thus positive depth of A means its supremum of regular sequence lengths is positive. If no element of maximalIdeal A were regular, every regular sequence in that ideal would be empty, bounding the supremum by zero, a contradiction. The first term of a nonempty regular sequence is regular. This is the private helper exists_regular_of_depth_pos. Ring equivalences identify the maximal ideals and regular sequences, hence preserve ring depths (depth_eq_of_ringEquiv).

For a regular x in the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring A, apply depth_quotSMulTop_of_isSMulRegular to the module A. Identify the submodule x smul top with Ideal.span {x}; the quotient is therefore A/(x) as an A-module. Its annihilation by (x) is checked on representatives. Apply depth_over_quotient_ring to identify its A-module depth with its quotient-ring depth. The finite natural-number depth equalities yield depth(A)=depth(A/(x))+1. This is depth_principal_quotient.

If the closed fibre F=S/m_R S has positive depth, choose a regular x in its maximal ideal. Lift x to y in S; the quotient maximal-ideal comap equality puts y in m_S. Use Ideal.smul_top_eq_map and Submodule.Quotient.restrictScalarsEquiv to identify S/m_R S as the R-module quotient used by flat_mod_injective. Multiplication by y reduces to multiplication by x, whose injectivity is the regularity hypothesis. Apply flat_mod_injective to obtain regularity of y on S and R-flatness of its cokernel. Identify the range of multiplication with (y), transporting flatness to S/(y). Set J=0 and K=(y), and compose R/0 equiv R with the quotient of the original map. Both quotients are nonzero and local. The quotient map is local and flat. The image of m_(R/0) in S/K equals the image of m_R S; DoubleQuot.quotQuotEquivComm and the equality K.map(S to F)=(x) identify the new fibre with F/(x). This is the completely proved private helper exists_fibre_regular_flat_quotients.

If depth(F) is not positive it is zero, and positivity of the original sum gives positive depth(R). Choose regular x in m_R. Set J=(x) and K=(phi(x)); Ideal.map_span gives J.map phi=K. Use Ideal.quotientMap for psi. Map/comap calculations with maximal ideals and the commuting quotient square prove locality. Mathlib IsSMulRegular.of_flat transports regular multiplication by x to regular multiplication by phi(x). Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor identifies S/J S with (R/J) tensor S as an R/J-algebra. The flat base-change instance and the quotient equivalence induced by J.map phi=K prove psi.Flat. Since K is contained in m_R S, DoubleQuot.quotQuotEquivQuotOfLE identifies the new fibre with F, and transports its local structure. This is the completely proved private helper exists_source_regular_flat_quotients.

Mathlib Ideal.Quotient.isNoetherianRing provides Noetherianity of every quotient used in the depth calculations. In the fibre case apply depth_principal_quotient to S,y and F,x, identify depth(R/0)=depth(R) and the new fibre depth via ring equivalences, and reassociate addition in Nat infinity. In the source case apply depth_principal_quotient to R,x and S,phi(x), identify the unchanged fibre depth, and commute and reassociate addition (ac_rfl). The quotient-square equality and all local and flat witnesses are supplied explicitly. This yields exactly both successor equalities of the original statement, without the flat local depth formula.

lean.statement: theorem exists_depth_reducing_flat_local_quotients {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] (φ : R →+* S) [IsLocalHom φ] (hflat : φ.Flat) [IsLocalRing (S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map φ)] (hpos : 0 < depth (R := R) R + depth (R := S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map φ) (S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map φ)) : ∃ (J : Ideal R) (K : Ideal S) (hJ : J ≤ maximalIdeal R) (hK : K ≤ maximalIdeal S), letI : Nontrivial (R ⧸ J) := Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff.mpr (ne_top_of_le_ne_top (maximalIdeal.isMaximal R).ne_top hJ) letI : Nontrivial (S ⧸ K) := Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff.mpr (ne_top_of_le_ne_top (maximalIdeal.isMaximal S).ne_top hK) letI : IsLocalRing (R ⧸ J) := IsLocalRing.of_surjective' (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective letI : IsLocalRing (S ⧸ K) := IsLocalRing.of_surjective' (Ideal.Quotient.mk K) Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective ∃ (ψ : (R ⧸ J) →+* (S ⧸ K)) (hψ : IsLocalHom ψ), ψ.Flat ∧ ∃ hF : IsLocalRing ((S ⧸ K) ⧸ (maximalIdeal (R ⧸ J)).map ψ), letI := hF ψ.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) = (Ideal.Quotient.mk K).comp φ ∧ depth (R := S) S = depth (R := S ⧸ K) (S ⧸ K) + 1 ∧ depth (R := R) R + depth (R := S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map φ) (S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map φ) = (depth (R := R ⧸ J) (R ⧸ J) + depth (R := (S ⧸ K) ⧸ (maximalIdeal (R ⧸ J)).map ψ) ((S ⧸ K) ⧸ (maximalIdeal (R ⧸ J)).map ψ)) + 1
